edits.stem: 27-year-old woman, 6 days after escaping a house fire sure neighbors set it to kill her; hears them whispering no nightmares, flashbacks or avoidance; no drug use; fully well 10 days later urine toxicology negative · T 36.8 °C
edits.companion: delusions and hallucinations after a marked stressor, with full return to baseline within a month, are brief psychotic disorder; acute stress disorder brings intrusion, negative mood, dissociation, avoidance and arousal, and she has no flashbacks, nightmares or avoidance; delusional disorder needs a delusion for 1 month or more
edits.lead_in: Which of the following is the most likely diagnosis?

edits.stem: 41-year-old man at a clinic visit hears voices, feels watched mood normal for 2 months manic and depressive episodes most of the past 15 years, each with voices and a persecutory belief urine toxicology negative · T 36.7 °C
edits.companion: voices and a persecutory belief during manic and depressive episodes, voices 2 weeks or more with a normal mood, and mood episodes over most of the illness are schizoaffective disorder, bipolar type; in bipolar I disorder the psychosis occurs only during mood episodes, and in schizophrenia mood episodes fill only a small part of the illness
edits.d1: Bipolar I disorder with psychotic features

edits.stem: 34-year-old woman, 5 months of unexpected spells: choking, nausea, chills, shaking each peaks within minutes and ends; no symptoms between spells dreads the next spell and fears a hidden disease; no drug use HR 74/min · TSH, glucose, ECG, toxicology normal
edits.companion: unexpected spells that peak within minutes and clear completely, with worry about further attacks, are panic disorder; in somatic symptom disorder the physical symptoms persist over time, and generalized anxiety disorder needs excessive worry about multiple issues, not only about the attacks
